task: Revalidate shared storefront engines E1-E11 and E13 against the current Mercedes-Maybach-Brabus stack with engine-specific adversarial proof, promote only engines whose required invariants are freshly proven, preserve each existing authority boundary, and keep Template #3 authoring forbidden until the separate final end-to-end Brabus rehearsal passes.

exceptions.reason: Intentional fail-closed undeclared-Blueprint branch. template3AuthoringReady must remain false when no Generator Blueprint is declared; this consumer is independent of the now-PROVEN Brabus engine revalidation maturity for declared generator candidates.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: The current production maturity catalog still blocks Template #3 because E1-E11 and E13 are all EVOLVE in the dedicated Brabus revalidation registry. Every engine already has canonical implementation and retained proof, so the missing capability is not another engine layer but fresh current-stack adversarial proof. This wave must prove each engine independently against its registered invariants, preserve its existing authority and mutation boundary, and promote only the engines that pass. A failure must identify the exact engine and trigger a separate targeted implementation fix rather than broadening this proof-only wave across multiple commerce/content/checkout authorities. During exact-head closure proof, the canonical Template Factory pull-request workflow returned SUCCESS while its own manifest marked gaming.playroom browserMatrixComplete=false (18/42 canary cases, no reusable previous full proof). The external completion handoff correctly rejected that artifact. This proves a gap inside the existing Template Factory gate: PR acceptance fallback can emit regression-signal canary evidence yet still exit success. The repair must align the existing gate with its declared 14x3 PR acceptance contract, not weaken external completion evidence.
observableOutcomes: A dedicated Brabus revalidation proof exercises E1-E11 adversarially through their existing public authorities without production mutation.
E13 remains on the existing exact-head browser/network checkout proof path and is never replaced by a synthetic unit-only proof.
Each revalidation row is PROVEN only when its current-stack proof producer exists and the engine-specific required invariants are explicitly exercised.
Retained proof alone cannot change an EVOLVE row to PROVEN.
Deterministic engines prove repeatability under input reordering and fail closed on malformed, stale, ineligible or incompatible inputs as appropriate.
Content authority proves publication/provenance/unsafe-content boundaries without moving content ownership into the Builder.
Server-read-model engines prove server-authoritative snapshots and reject unsafe/tampered state instead of recomputing price, tax, stock or order constraints client-side.
E13 exact-head proof preserves authoritative quote, shared runtime and guided checkout behavior without production side effects.
No engine source file is changed in the initial proof-first transaction.
If any engine fails revalidation, its state remains EVOLVE/RETHINK and the failure is split into a targeted engine repair wave before revalidation resumes.

Technical production maturity may become Template3AuthoringReady only when every engine row is PROVEN, but actual Template #3 authoring remains forbidden until the separate final end-to-end Brabus rehearsal passes.
When a pull-request exact-head run has no reusable complete proof for a non-factory template, fallback selection is full rather than canary.
Push-only regression runs may retain default canary fallback when no full prior proof exists.
A pull-request Template Factory run fails closed if any selected acceptance proof remains browserMatrixComplete=false or browserMatrixPassed=false.
The external proof handoff contract remains unchanged and continues to require complete exact-head acceptance evidence.
unresolvedRisks: A retained regression test may be mistaken for fresh Brabus revalidation.
One consolidated proof may accidentally hide an engine-specific missing invariant.
A deterministic engine may pass happy-path tests but fail under input reordering or malformed state.
A commerce read-model proof may accidentally mutate authoritative commerce state.
E10 may accept unverifiable provenance or unsafe content.
E11 may silently recompute server-owned price/tax/stock data.
E13 may be falsely promoted from unit evidence without the exact-head browser/network journey.
Registry promotion may mark all engines PROVEN even when one proof producer is absent.
Template #3 authoring may start immediately after technical maturity without the separate final rehearsal.
A future scope-selection change could accidentally reintroduce canary-only PR acceptance.
Making every push run full would unnecessarily increase proof cost; the correction must distinguish PR acceptance from push regression signaling.

in: Dedicated current-stack Brabus revalidation contract for E1-E11 and E13.
Engine-by-engine adversarial proof of the existing requiredInvariants registry.
Determinism, malformed-state, stale-state, authority-boundary and no-production-mutation proof where applicable.
Exact-head E13 browser/network proof linkage through the existing Template Factory handoff authority.
Revalidation registry promotion only for freshly proven engines.
Production maturity and Generator Readiness regression proof for the resulting engine blocker set.
Repair the existing Template Factory PR fallback so missing reusable proof triggers a full browser matrix.
Fail closed at the existing Template Factory gate when PR acceptanceProofs are incomplete.
out: New parallel engine implementations or duplicate commerce/content/checkout authorities.
Changing engine product code before a revalidation test demonstrates a concrete deficiency.
Weakening release risk, knowledge, Template Factory or Completion Truth gates.
Replacing E13 browser proof with synthetic unit evidence.
Production database, payment, order, inventory or customer mutation.
Template #3 authoring before the final end-to-end Brabus rehearsal.
Weakening external proof handoff completeness requirements.
Forcing all push regression runs to execute full 14x3 matrices.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: These proof rows gate the final technical readiness of Template Production. Highest practical assurance is fresh executable engine-specific adversarial evidence, deterministic replay, malformed/stale/fail-closed cases, explicit authority and no-mutation boundaries, exact-head browser proof for E13, and fail-closed registry promotion. Existing retained proof is useful baseline knowledge but is not itself sufficient for Brabus promotion.

acceptanceCriteria: The revalidation registry retains exactly E1-E11 and E13 and no reserved E12 row is introduced.
Every PROVEN revalidation row has a non-null proofProducer distinct from the fact of retained proof.
E1 proves canonical Page Schema/runtime validation, binding resolution, responsive behavior and registry authority under invalid and valid inputs.
E2 proves deterministic explainable discovery, ineligible exclusion and no commerce mutation under candidate/input reordering.
E3 proves deterministic guidance, evidence explanation, invalid selection rejection and template-switch authority preservation.
E4 proves real-catalog-line composition, atomic intent, server revalidation and no silent replacement.
E5 proves slot validation, compatibility fail-closed, server revalidation and no silent replacement.
E6 proves structured evidence, explainability, UNKNOWN not compatible and malformed-rule fail-closed behavior.
E7 proves shared structured registry, unit normalization, comparison determinism and no commerce mutation.
E8 proves customer-context separation, soft ranking rather than hard lock, cart preservation and server persistence authority.
E9 proves server retention evidence, current-commerce revalidation, no invented subscription and no silent quantity adjustment.
E10 proves publication lifecycle, provenance fail-closed, unsafe-content rejection and template-switch content preservation.
E11 proves server-authoritative snapshot usage, no client recomputation of price/tax/stock, MOQ/order-multiple preservation and unsafe snapshot fail-closed.
E13 is PROVEN only with the existing exact-head browser/network checkout proof that shows shared runtime, authoritative quote, guided checkout and no production side effect.
Any failed engine remains non-PROVEN and identifies a targeted follow-up repair; the registry cannot bulk-promote around a failing proof.
Production maturity removes only engine blockers whose proof passed.
Template #3 authoring remains separately forbidden until the final end-to-end Brabus rehearsal passes.
On GITHUB_EVENT_NAME=pull_request with no reusable prior proof, non-factory templates select mode=full and all canonical page types.
On non-PR push fallback with no reusable prior proof, non-factory templates may remain mode=canary.
A PR manifest containing any acceptance proof with browserMatrixComplete=false or browserMatrixPassed=false makes the Template Factory gate fail.
The correction is covered by the existing Template Factory gate regression test and by this PR's next exact-head workflow, which must produce complete Playroom and Loot Vault acceptance evidence.
invariants: Retained proof is not fresh Brabus proof.
One engine failure cannot be hidden by other engine passes.
Proof cannot create a new engine authority.
Commerce/content/checkout ownership remains with the registered authority.
No revalidation proof mutates production state.
Template #3 final rehearsal remains mandatory after technical maturity.
Canary browser evidence is a regression signal, never sufficient PR acceptance evidence.
External completion handoff completeness is not weakened to compensate for incomplete upstream evidence.

failureModes: A proof file merely checks version constants and never exercises the registered invariant.
One test loops engines generically and falsely treats shared PASS as engine-specific proof.
Candidate order changes ranking output for a deterministic engine.
Malformed compatibility/configuration data is accepted as valid.
A B2B read model recomputes a server-owned commercial value.
Unsafe editorial markup or unverifiable provenance reaches the public read model.
E13 is marked PROVEN before exact-head checkout proof exists.
Registry state changes to PROVEN while proofProducer remains null.
Technical readiness is misinterpreted as authorization to build Template #3.
edgeCases: Identical deterministic candidates supplied in reversed order.
Empty or malformed engine input that previously never reached a happy-path test.
Stale server snapshot or missing authoritative field.
Unknown compatibility result alongside otherwise valid data.
Valid content mixed with one unsafe relation or provenance claim.
E13 exact-head browser proof succeeds while a unit-only registry assertion also exists.
Eleven engines pass and one engine fails.

alternatives.summary: Fresh engine-specific adversarial proof over existing authorities; repair only engines that demonstrate a concrete deficiency.
alternatives.reason: Maximizes evidence while minimizing unnecessary cross-authority implementation change and release risk.

alternatives.summary: Mark EVOLVE rows PROVEN because retained engine tests already pass.
alternatives.reason: Would collapse historical proof and current Brabus revalidation into the same claim and permit false readiness.

alternatives.summary: Rewrite or harden every engine before testing.
alternatives.reason: Creates unnecessary multi-authority change, exceeds practical release-risk discipline and may introduce regressions without evidence of deficiency.

specialistReviews.finding: The functional registry is already the canonical engine map and should remain the only maturity linkage.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extend only the Brabus revalidation evidence rows; do not create a second engine registry.

specialistReviews.finding: Retained proof and new revalidation proof can point at similar code paths and accidentally double-count evidence.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require dedicated revalidation assertions for every registered invariant and keep retainedProofProducer separate from current proofProducer.

specialistReviews.finding: This wave changes no storefront presentation; its only UX effect is whether Template Production can progress.
specialistReviews.resolution: Keep Template #3 authoring process-blocked until the later end-to-end rehearsal despite technical maturity.

specialistReviews.finding: Changing multiple engine implementations in one PR would exceed the intended proof-only release envelope.
specialistReviews.resolution: Initial wave edits only Builder registry/maturity plus tests. Any failing engine gets a separate targeted repair transaction before revalidation resumes.

challenge.scenario: All retained proof suites are green.
challenge.finding: Historical PASS does not prove current Brabus adversarial invariants.
challenge.resolution: Rows remain EVOLVE until dedicated current revalidation evidence passes.

challenge.scenario: Eleven engines pass and E6 fails malformed-rule handling.
challenge.finding: Bulk promotion would hide one unsafe engine.
challenge.resolution: E6 remains non-PROVEN and blocks Template #3 while the eleven proven rows may retain their evidence.

challenge.scenario: E2 produces the same set but different order when candidates are reversed.
challenge.resolution: Revalidation fails and no registry promotion occurs for E2.

challenge.scenario: E10 contains one unverifiable provenance relation among valid content.
challenge.finding: Partial validity cannot override provenance failure.

challenge.scenario: E11 snapshot omits or tampers a server-owned commercial field.
challenge.resolution: Reject unsafe snapshot; never fill price/tax/stock locally.

challenge.scenario: Unit tests for E13 are green but no exact-head browser handoff exists.
challenge.resolution: E13 remains EVOLVE until GUARD-TEMPLATE-FACTORY exact-head browser proof passes.

challenge.scenario: All engine rows become technically PROVEN.
challenge.finding: This does not satisfy the separate full-system Brabus rehearsal.
challenge.resolution: Template #3 authoring stays process-blocked until the next rehearsal wave closes.

challenge.scenario: A revalidation proof passes functionally but mutates its input object, cart-like state, catalog fixture or story fixture during evaluation.
challenge.finding: A PASS with hidden mutation would violate the registered no-production-mutation/read-model boundary and could make repeated proof order-dependent.
challenge.resolution: Adversarial tests snapshot/freeze relevant inputs and assert immutability or stable replay; any mutation leaves the engine non-PROVEN and triggers a targeted repair wave.

challenge.scenario: A PR changes only engine registry/tests, there is no reusable complete Playroom checkpoint, and fallback scope selection chooses six canary pages.
challenge.finding: The browser runner may report no case errors and exit zero even though acceptanceProof.browserMatrixComplete=false (18/42), producing a workflow SUCCESS that cannot satisfy Completion Truth.
challenge.resolution: On pull_request fallback, select full pages for every template lacking reusable complete proof and add a final fail-closed PR acceptance check over acceptanceProofs. Preserve canary fallback only for non-PR regression runs.
